J1.evidence: Source: «فبالفكر وحده يحيا الإنسان وبالفكر استدل على وجوده». The pronoun in «وجوده» is grammatically ambiguous: it can refer to God (context: «ويشهد لمن أبدعها بالحول والطّول والانفراد بالوحدانية») or to man himself (parallel subject الإنسان, and the later Descartes allusion «ومن الغزالي وديكارت» suggests the cogito: by thought man proved his own existence). TR commits to God («O'nun varlığına») without a note. Not demonstrably wrong but not certain; needs scholarly judgement whether to keep the ambiguity or mark the interpretation in a Mütercim notu.

J2.evidence: The flagged «استدل على وجوده» -> 'he infers His existence' is right (antecedent is المنعم / من أبدعها). J1.evidence: Source: «فبالفكر وحده يحيا الإنسان وبالفكر استدل على وجوده». Also the past tense استدل is rendered present "infers". Not certainly wrong; a lowercase "his" would preserve the ambiguity. Needs scholarly decision.

J1.evidence: Arabic «فهو لم يقصد من التماسه من صاحبيه أن يكتما عن سيف الدولة ... رفقا به وحذرا» most naturally parses with أن يكتما as object of التماسه and رفقا/حذرا as object of يقصد (likely a dropped إلا in the source). EN 'He did not mean, in asking his two companions to conceal..., to be gentle with him and to fear' follows that parse and translates what is written, negation included; it does not alter the text. A note would help but its absence is not an error under the rules.

J2.evidence: Arabic «فهو لم يقصد من التماسه من صاحبيه أن يكتما ... رفقا به وحذرا أن يدفعه الشوق» - context (Mutanabbi forbidding them to tell Sayf al-Dawla lest he rush into danger) shows the concealment was out of gentleness; the text is evidently defective (missing إلا). EN 'He did not mean ... to be gentle with him and to fear' publishes the opposite of the passage's point with no Translator's note; needs a literal rendering plus a note, as TR has.

J3.evidence: Arabic «فهو لم يقصد من التماسه من صاحبيه أن يكتما عن سيف الدولة ما سمعاه ... رفقا به وحذرا أن يدفعه الشوق» negates the intent that they conceal (out of kindness and caution). EN «He did not mean, in asking his two companions to conceal ..., to be gentle with him and to fear ...» makes the concealment the presupposed request and moves the negation onto the motive (gentleness/fear). That says something the Arabic does not say and contradicts the passage's point. The source's evidently problematic «لم يقصد» also gets no Translator's note (TR has one). Fix: translate literally ('He did not intend, by his request to his two companions, that they conceal ... out of kindness to him and caution ...') and add a [Translator's note: ...] on the apparent contradiction.
